decision: Registered rejection met: the H01 anatomy does not spike at 200 pA, so there is no upstroke reading. Recorded as a count contrast of the input.

reading.mesh_control: nseg 1 gives 653 V/s against 598 at nseg 9 (9.3 percent, inside the 10 percent band); count 4, first spike 126.5 ms, threshold -57.4 mV: the mesh moves the upstroke but nothing else.
reading.h01_anatomy: No spike. Rest -85.8 mV (donor -84.0); plateau -78.2 mV at 200 pA against the donor's -64 to -65 mV; onset capacitance 785 pF against 125 pF; input resistance about 38 MOhm from the plateau (donor about 98). The converted skeleton (2460 um of cable, 9975 nodes, 8551 sections) is a far larger load than the Allen reconstruction.
reading.interpretation: The input branch (cable load) can move the 200 pA response by far more than any function lever tested, but this change was too large to read the upstroke: an isolation split needs a change that keeps the Y observable (Hartshorne: contrasts must stay within the observable range). Whether the H01 load is physical or inflated by the conversion (skeleton radii as cable radii, spine-corrected cm 2.3 on 2460 um) is not established here.

next: A graded input change on the donor anatomy that keeps spiking: scale the dendritic membrane area (cm and g_pas together, i.e. the cable load) by 1.5 and 2, read the upstroke and the 200 pA count; and separately check the H01 conversion's membrane area against the H01 surface mesh before using that skeleton again.
